statement: Input scope cannot be recovered from a results row's own text: classifying all 520 rows of the 8 research lines by their path-shaped command and source fields left 438 rows unknown, 79 fixture and 3 real, and the one claim the classifier flagged as fixture-presented-as-real was flagged because its experiment directory is named 'probe', not because of its data.
falsification: Classify the same 520 rows by a rule that reads only the row text and see the unknown bucket fall to a small share, or see a fixture-presented-as-real claim flagged for a reason other than its directory name.

statement: The layer holds no notion of what a measurement was taken on: neither hooks/tezgah_research.py nor hooks/tezgah_integrity.py contains a scope, fixture or stand-in field or rule, and the checker's only provenance requirement on a row is the source field that says where the row came from.
falsification: Show a rule in either module that reads, requires or refuses an input-scope field on a results row or a claim.

statement: A number-in-the-proof rule is mostly inside tolerance rather than mostly violated: of the 76 claims across 7 lines whose statement carries a number, 63 (83 percent) have every number present verbatim in the artifacts they cite, so the rule would refuse 17 percent of claims that are not wrong and belongs in the checker's warning class.
falsification: Re-run the containment probe on the same claims and see fewer than two thirds contained, which would make even the warning class noise.

statement: Making an over-claim decidable rather than judged requires the harness to have written the expected value in advance: a capped evaluation detects cheating because a non-cheating run cannot exceed a bound the harness chose, and nothing in the run afterwards recovers that bound.
falsification: Find a published scheme that detects an over-claim from the artifacts of the run alone, with no value fixed before it.

statement: An integrity rule written only as prompt prose does not bind: the 100-agent swarm study lists forbidden constructs in its system prompt and records that the rule was not actively enforced beyond its automated checks, with the cheating reconstructed afterwards from an unmonitored log channel.
falsification: Find a record of a prompt-stated integrity rule that bound without any mechanical check behind it.

statement: Judge-free detection by construction is the transferable mechanism for this class: a stand-in whose expected value the harness itself wrote makes 'this number came from the real system' a decidable mismatch instead of a judgement an LLM evaluator has to make.
falsification: Show that a planted-expectation control is either impossible to keep out of what is being measured, or that a judge is required to decide the comparison.

statement: The containment rule as it ships - the checker's own NUMBER tokenizer over the text of the files a proof names - leaves 53 of 71 numeric claims fully contained (75 percent) in the pass recorded as refined-tokenizer, so a hard refusal would refuse a quarter of the claims that are not wrong; the first pass's 83 percent described a rule whose evidence also included whole directories the claim never cited, which is why the rule's own pass is the number spec.md uses.
falsification: Run the checker's own tokenizer and artifact reader over this line's claims and get a containment share outside 70 to 80 percent.

statement: The presentation half of the class is refused by the layer now: a claim declaring scope real over rows that all record fixture is refused by check, the write path refuses the same claim so the two judges agree, and a claim resting on fixture rows that declares no scope warns and is refused under strict.
falsification: Show a claim that declares real over all-fixture rows which check --strict accepts, or a write path that records what check would refuse.

statement: The scope field is produced where it can only be produced: a results row may declare real, fixture or derived, an off-vocabulary value is refused, a missing one is reported once per file with the count, and source --run --scope lets the filer declare it at the point of filing rather than reconstructing it later.
falsification: Show a row whose scope is recovered by a rule instead of declared, or a way to file a run whose scope is set without the filer stating it.

statement: The class is visible to the reader who opens nothing else: status prints each line's fixture-scoped claims by id, and the report of a concluded line that carries one must contain the word fixture anywhere in it.
falsification: Show a line whose claims rest on fixture rows that status reports without naming them, or a report rule that passes a report never mentioning the fixture.

statement: Statement-level provenance is the published remedy for this class and not this line's invention: a receipt-based audit of frontier agentic QA records a production incident in which fabricated structural claims were mixed with accurate numeric tables, and concludes that the burden of proof has to move from the model to the evidence trail.
falsification: Find a published audit of the class that recommends an answer-level check instead of a claim-level receipt.

statement: The stand-in class is now partly enforced rather than only named: a result row whose scope is fixture must also carry the text naming what was generated, a missing one is warned once per file with the count and refused under strict, and source --run --fixture lets the filer state it, so the tool cannot file a row its own checker warns about.
falsification: Show a fixture row with no description that check --strict accepts, or a way to file one with the tool that leaves it undescribed.

statement: The containment rule as it finally ships leaves 80 of 82 numeric claims contained, and the two it warns about are a row one line superseded with a 4400 figure and a row another line superseded with a 2,019 figure, both kept visible on purpose; it stays a warning rather than a gate because its match is a substring, so a pass is not proof.
falsification: Run the shipped rule over the tree and see more than two warned claims, or see a warning whose numbers are all present in the artifacts it cites.

statement: The undeclared-scope debt is closed and was measured on both sides: 510 of this repository's 813 result rows declared no scope before the pass, and 0 of 822 declare none after it, with 371 fixture rows naming what was generated and 0 that do not.
falsification: Count the rows again and find one that declares no scope, or a fixture row that does not say what was generated.

statement: A session whose only passing check ran a scratch or stand-in path is now reminded that its evidence is about the code path: the reminder names the command, fires only when no passing check ran against a real path, and is dropped by the verify-off switch that already owns the integrity rule.
falsification: Show a session with a passing check against a real path that still gets the reminder, or a session whose only passing check ran in a scratch path that does not.
